title: Humanoid Robots Are Changing Work in 2026

slides.heading: Humanoid Robots Are Changing Work in 2026
slides.body: From factory floors to warehouses, human-shaped robots are entering real workplaces at an unprecedented pace.

slides.heading: Why Humanoid? The Design Logic
slides.body: Our world is built for humans — doors, stairs, tools, vehicles. Humanoid robots can navigate these spaces without redesigning the environment, giving them a practical edge over specialized machines.

slides.heading: Key Players Racing Ahead
slides.body: Figure AI, Unitree, Agility Robotics, and Tesla's Optimus are deploying units at scale. BMW, Amazon, and GE Aerospace have signed pilot agreements, putting humanoids on active production lines.

slides.heading: What They Can Do Today
slides.body: Current humanoids handle repetitive pick-and-place tasks, pallet loading, parts inspection, and basic assembly. Dexterous hands now achieve near-human grasp success rates above 95% on structured tasks.

slides.heading: The AI Brain Behind the Body
slides.body: Large action models — trained on millions of hours of human motion data — let robots generalize new tasks from a handful of demonstrations. They no longer need months of custom programming for each job.

slides.heading: Cost vs. Human Labor
slides.body: Lease rates are falling toward $10–15 per hour for a fully operational unit. At that price point, humanoids become economically competitive for shift-based, physically demanding roles in high-wage markets.

slides.heading: Workforce Impact: Displacement or Collaboration?
slides.body: Economists see a split outcome — routine physical jobs face automation pressure, while roles requiring judgment, communication, and flexibility are expected to grow. Companies are retraining workers as robot supervisors and technicians.

slides.heading: Safety and Regulation
slides.body: OSHA and the EU AI Act are establishing new rules for human-robot collaboration zones. Robots must pass rigorous force-limit and emergency-stop tests before sharing a workspace with people.

slides.heading: What Comes Next: 2027 and Beyond
slides.body: Analysts project over one million humanoid units deployed globally by 2028. The next frontier is unstructured environments — healthcare support, construction sites, and elder care — where adaptability matters most.

slides.heading: The Robot Colleague Is Already Here
slides.body: Humanoid robots aren't a distant sci-fi promise — they are clocking in today. Understanding how they work, where they excel, and how they reshape labor is essential knowledge for anyone thinking about the future of work.
